submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a token that is a spelling chunk of a longer word which is still unfinished: a word-initial or mid-word chunk of a multi-token, low-frequency Latinate word ('oc' in 'autocorrect', 'ic' in 'Unicode', 'umer' in 'enumerates', 'ob' in 'protobuf', 'enumer'/'navig'/'evapor' stems). The same fragment token barely fires when it is the word's final chunk or when the word is a single token ('ic' 2.28 in 'Unicode' vs 0.30 as the last chunk of 'gothic'; 'oc' 4.40 in 'autocorrect' vs 0.68 as the last chunk of 'havoc'), and activation is unchanged whichever closing chunk follows (enumerates/enumerated/enumeration), so it is retrospective: its output direction pushes the word's closing chunks (-ates, -ate, -ated, -ately) but it encodes 'a word is being spelled out', not the specific next token; extremely rare all-caps name tokens such as 'GNU' (up to 4.4) are the main exception.
